anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet the ESP32-C3-MINI-1 (U8) pin 15 (GPIO9) carries the shared SPI read-back net NET0017, and pin 16 (GPIO10) is drawn with a no-connect 'X'. NET0017 is the same label that appears on the SO (pin 7, MISO) of all three MAX31855KASA devices (U1/U9/U6) on the Thermocouples sheet, so MISO is routed to GPIO9 and GPIO10 is left unused.
anomalies.expected: The intended design places the thermocouple MISO on GPIO10: 'SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7' and 'SO (pin 7, tri-state/MISO) are common nets (SCK, SO) tied to all three ICs and to the ESP32 (U1 GPIO5/SCK, GPIO10/SO)'.

anomalies.impact: The shipped firmware clocks and reads the MAX31855 bus on GPIO5/GPIO10; with MISO physically on GPIO9 and GPIO10 floating, every thermocouple read fails and the firmware raises a ThermocoupleFault, so a run can never proceed and the heater is kept off.

anomalies.observed: The WS2812B status LED (D7) data input DIN (pin 4) is wired to net label NET0004 on the Microcontroller sheet. NET0004 is the same net that runs from the ESP32-C3-MINI-1 pin 13 (GPIO1) to the TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 heater switch U3 pins 1 (IN) and 2 (DIAG_EN), and to the heater indicator circuit J5/D10/R12.
anomalies.expected: The status-LED data line must be a dedicated GPIO net of its own; the WS2812B is an independent status indicator and the heater is switched from GPIO1, so the two signals must not share a net.

evidence.quote: Microcontroller sheet: U3 'DIAG_EN 2' and 'IN 1' both wired to label 'NET0004'; U8 pin 13 (GPIO1) wired to label 'NET0004'; D7 'WS2812B' pin '4 (DIN)' wired to label 'NET0004'
Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1
a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1)

anomalies.impact: The ~800 kHz WS2812B serial data stream would also be applied to the smart high-side switch's IN/DIAG_EN pins, causing the heater to toggle erratically (or to be driven by LED data), while the LED receives only the static heater logic level instead of a valid data frame — both the heater control and the status LED are corrupted.
